name: Maurya Empire

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 4.0 million km2 (high). The historical-basemaps world_bc300 polygon (nearest file at or before -250 holding the polity) measures 1.95 million km2 on the sphere (computed from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_bc300.geojson, low); it predates the Kalinga conquest (c. 261 BCE) and the southern extension. Mid 3.0M is between; older textbook figures of 5M include loosely held periphery.

population.note: Dyson (2018, p. 24, quoted on the page): South Asia in Mauryan times (320-220 BCE) held 15-30 million; Sumit Guha treats 20 million as an upper limit. The empire covered most but not all of that (Tamil south and forest tribes outside), mid 22M; high 35M allows for older estimates (50-60M, e.g. HYDE India year 0 = 75M via OWID) that this file treats as too high. Seshat codes an unusable 15.5-181M range (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/87).

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Pataliputra 50,000-270,000 (Seshat 87, uncertain), Taxila, Ujjain and other Ganges cities; overwhelmingly rural.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Megasthenes via Pliny gives Chandragupta 600,000 infantry, 30,000 cavalry, 8,000 chariots and 9,000 elephants (ancient claim, quoted on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_elephant); rejected as a mid. Kalinga alone is credited with 60,000 infantry, 1,000 cavalry and 700 elephants (same page). ~1% of a 22M population is the mid.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Guild (sreni) militias, allied and forest-tribe contingents reachable within a month.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Mahouts and crews for ~2,500 elephants (2-3 each), chariot crews, the six war-office boards, commissariat and river transport.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Salaried standing army plus guild (sreni) and forest-tribe levies named in the Arthashastra; a few percent of the population is the ceiling for an agrarian empire of this kind.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Spear and shield infantry of the salaried army; share of the active-force guess.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical). Evidence: iron spears and swords, little body armour

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: paid standing troops under the Arthashastra boards

count.note: Educated guess. Archers with the long bamboo bow described by Megasthenes/Arrian; share of the active-force guess.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: powerful but slow long bow

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: standing archers

count.note: Educated guess. Hired (bhrta) light troops in state pay.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: light weapons

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: paid troops

count.note: Educated guess. Horse; Pliny claims 30,000 (high). Indian cavalry was light and secondary to elephants.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 minus. Evidence: small horses, no stirrups

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: standing troops

count.note: Educated guess. Pliny/Megasthenes claim 8,000 (high); chariots were already declining in Indian warfare.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: heavy four-horse chariots, a generation behind

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: board of chariots in the war office

count.note: Educated guess. Platform count. Ancient claim 9,000 (Megasthenes/Pliny, high) and 500 ceded to Seleucus c. 303 BCE, called a small part of the Mauryan force (both on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_elephant).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: largest elephant corps of the age, superintendent of elephants (gajadhyaksha)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: elephant sanctuaries and specialist trainers per the Arthashastra

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: centralised war office of 30 members in six boards (Megasthenes); Kalinga conquered c. 261

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: salaried standing army paid from the treasury (Arthashastra), allied contingents less cohesive

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5. Evidence: Ashoka renounced conquest after Kalinga; no major war in progress

weapons.note: Anchor: 3 (300 BCE iron weapons). Evidence: iron swords and spears, long bamboo bow; no torsion artillery attested in use

armor.note: Anchor: between 2 (bronze scale) and 3. Evidence: Arthashastra lists armour types, but Greek sources describe lightly armoured troops

ships.note: Anchor: between 2 and 3. Evidence: superintendent of ships; river and coastal craft on the Ganges and the Bay of Bengal

fortification.note: Anchor: 3 (ashlar walls, siege towers). Evidence: Pataliputra timber wall with 64 gates and 570 towers (Megasthenes, on the Maurya page)

logistics.note: Anchor: 3 (engineered roads, depots). Evidence: Uttarapatha road Bengal to Taxila, state granaries and storehouses

communications.note: Anchor: 3 (mounted relay posts). Evidence: courier system and edicts posted across the empire

isr.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: extensive spy network prescribed by the Arthashastra audit 2026-10-30: mid 3.1 -> 3.03, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for -250 (3.032); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID grapher CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) has no India value before 1600 (1,264); its year-1 values are Egypt 1,116, Iran 1,116, Belgium/France 956 (2011 int$). Ancient South Asia placed in that band.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Large salaried army and elephant establishment paid from land revenue; no budget survives.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. State workshops, mining and guild crafts in a mostly agrarian economy.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Fertile Ganges plain with rice double-cropping; state granaries.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. The Uttarapatha ran ~2,500 km from Bengal to Taxila; other roads linked the Narmada basin and the south (Stein, on the Maurya page).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Coastal and Bay of Bengal trade craft; no figures.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Ox-cart and elephant trains; armies operated within the road network.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Oxen, buffalo and some horses across a 22M agrarian population.

homeDefense.note: 1.1 (familiar terrain, local supply) to 1.2 (fortified cities like Pataliputra). Monsoon floods hamper invaders.

notes: Snapshot c. 250 BCE under Ashoka, after the Kalinga war (c. 261 BCE; Ashoka claims 100,000 killed and 150,000 deported, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalinga_War). Population convention: everything inside the empire, Dyson's low modern range for South Asia; older figures of 50-60 million are treated as the high end only. All army figures from Megasthenes, Pliny and Plutarch (600,000 infantry, 30,000 cavalry, 8,000-9,000 elephants) are ancient claims and only bound the high side. Elephants and chariots are platforms; mahouts and crews are in supportPersonnel. Border: world_bc300 is the nearest file at or before the year that contains the polity; it understates the extent (no Kalinga, no Deccan), so areaKm2 mid is researched, not the polygon. GDP per capita is a regional analogy (grade D). Ratings use the rubric in data/SOURCES.md. Personnel: active = the hereditary (maula) and hired (bhrta) troops in state pay with the royal elephants and chariots; trainedReserves = guild (sreni), allied and forest-tribe (atavi) levies; mobilizable = population x ratio.
